summary:

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: partially_preserved - preserve identity, age, body proportions, navy suit, white shirt, skin tone, and studio-photo realism while changing only the requested property in each cell.

detailed_description:
The target is one still image, not a video. Present exactly six equal-sized borderless photographs in a clean 3-column by 2-row grid on the same light gray studio background. Every cell must show the same recognizable adult man from <Picture 1>. Do not merge cells and do not omit any requested cell.

Top-left, Photo 1: keep the original frontal head-and-shoulders pose and proportions; change only the white dress shirt to a vivid red dress shirt, leaving the navy suit unchanged.
Top-middle, Photo 2: keep the original frontal head-and-shoulders pose, clothing, and proportions; make him smile naturally with closed lips and relaxed eyes.
Top-right, Photo 3: keep his identity, clothing, and proportions; reconstruct a strict clean right-side profile view, with only one eye and one cheek visible.
Bottom-left, Photo 4: show a complete full-body standing portrait from head to shoes, natural posture, navy suit and white shirt, both hands and both feet visible.
Bottom-middle, Photo 5: keep identity, clothing, frontal framing, and proportions; change only the hairstyle to a textured layered wolf cut, still black.
Bottom-right, Photo 6: keep identity, clothing, frontal framing, and proportions; add a tasteful black fashion fedora and thin black rectangular eyeglasses.

The image must contain exactly six panels and exactly one version of <Subject 1> per panel. Keep faces sharp and mutually consistent. No captions, labels, text, logos, borders, extra people, duplicate faces, merged bodies, extra limbs, distorted eyes, asymmetrical glasses, cropped feet in Photo 4, or motion.

nodes.title: Stage 1 Prompt · Identity / Body / Outfit Roles
widgets_values:
Create one static high-resolution character turnaround sheet of the same adult person from Picture 1.

IDENTITY AND BODY — Picture 1 has priority:
Preserve the facial identity, age, gender presentation, skin tone, hairstyle, and natural facial proportions from Picture 1. Use the body build visible in Picture 1 when available. If Picture 1 is face-only, infer a natural full-body build that matches the age and gender presentation of Picture 1.

OUTFIT ONLY — Picture 2:
Use Picture 2 only for the costume design, colors, materials, footwear, and wearable accessories. Apply those items to the person from Picture 1. Do not copy Picture 2's donor face, age, gender, shoulder width, muscle mass, torso volume, height, limb thickness, body shape, pose, or background. The character wears the costume; the character does not inherit the outfit donor's body. Keep the face uncovered; do not wear a helmet or mask.

Arrange exactly three equal vertical photographs from left to right on a neutral light-grey studio background:
Photo 1: complete full-body front view in a relaxed A-pose.
Photo 2: complete full-body strict 90-degree right-side view.
Photo 3: complete full-body back view.

Keep the same Picture 1 identity and body build, the same Picture 2 costume, scale, ground line, lighting, and realistic photographic finish in all three photos. Show the complete head and feet. No extra panel, no action pose, no separate product display, and no text.

nodes.title: Stage 2 Input Guide · Panel Count / Layout / Props
widgets_values:
# Stage 2 Inputs and Three-Panel Layout

1. Choose 1–4 images with **Panel Count**.
2. If you choose 3 panels, select a fixed **Three-Panel Layout**:
   - OFF: one tall panel on the left + two stacked panels on the right
   - ON: one wide panel on top + two panels along the bottom
3. The pose image is analyzed for Panel 1's action.
4. Prop Mode OFF displays the enabled prop separately; ON makes the character hold and use it.
5. Enable only the optional prop, environment, or accessory references you need.

Create one static high-resolution character contact sheet of the same adult character from Picture 1.

The SELECTED PANEL COUNT appended below is mandatory. Create exactly that many panels and no more:
- 1 panel: one full-canvas image.
- 2 panels: two equal side-by-side images.
- 3 panels: follow the selected THREE-PANEL LAYOUT PRESET appended below. Use exactly three cells; they are intentionally asymmetrical and do not need equal dimensions.
- 4 panels: a clean 2x2 grid.

Picture 1 is the fused Stage 1 character reference. Preserve its face, hair, costume, colors, materials, and body proportions in every character panel. Additional enabled pictures contribute only their named prop, accessory, or environment.

Default panel plan:
Panel 1: reproduce the analyzed action pose below as closely as possible, full body visible.
Panel 2: follow the selected PROP USAGE MODE below.
Panel 3: chest-up identity and costume-detail close-up, calm posture.
Panel 4: a clearly different cinematic or environment pose, or another user-requested utility view.

Use only Panels 1 through the selected count and ignore the unused higher-numbered defaults. Every active character panel must use a visibly different body arrangement and camera framing. Use a neutral light-grey studio background unless an enabled environment specifies otherwise. No duplicate or mirrored panel, no merged cell, no pasted source image, no extra person, and no text.

Start Here · Complete Workflow Guide
widgets_values:
# 🚀 Quick Start

1. Check all six required models in **① Model Setup**.
2. Read **② Stage 1 Inputs**, then load a face/identity image and an outfit/hair image.
3. Add an optional Stage 1 direction only when needed.
4. Queue the workflow and review the Stage 1 front / side / back sheet.
5. Read the Stage 2 guide and decide whether you need extra pose, prop, environment, or close-up panels.
6. Stage 2 is optional. Use the click toggle, configure the Stage 2 inputs, then queue again.

The default path is Stage 1 only. Stage 2 also creates the final horizontal 16:9 composite.

nodes.title: How to Use · Image Roles
widgets_values:
# Stage 1 Image Roles

- **Picture 1 — Face / Identity:** identity, age, gender presentation, hairstyle, and baseline body impression.
- **Picture 2 — Outfit Only:** costume design, colors, materials, footwear, and wearable items.

H3 can inherit the outfit donor's physique. For the most reliable result, use a mannequin, flat-lay, isolated garment image, or an outfit reference with less visible body shape.

To change the physique, type an English request in group **③**.
Example: `slender adult feminine build, narrower shoulders, slim torso and limbs`

The Stage 1 direction is applied at highest priority while Picture 1 remains the identity source and Picture 2 remains the outfit source. Do not add pose, prop, or environment references to Stage 1.

widgets_values_named.text:
# Stage 1 Image Roles

- **Face / Identity Image:** the character's facial identity.
- **Hair + Full Outfit Image:** hairstyle, outfit construction, materials, and color design.
- Stage 1 combines only these two references into one neutral studio turnaround sheet.
- Do not add pose, prop, or environment references to Stage 1.
- Output: front, side, and back views of the same character.

nodes.title: Output Structure · Stage 1 Default / Stage 2 Optional
widgets_values:
# Output Structure

- **Stage 2 OFF:** generates only the Stage 1 front / side / back sheet.
- **Stage 2 ON:** generates the selected 1–4 Stage 2 panels and a final horizontal 16:9 composite.
- The Stage 1 result is placed on the left and the Stage 2 result on the right.
- Preview and saved outputs are available in the result groups.

# 📦 6 Required Models

## Required Custom Nodes

Install both from ComfyUI Manager, then restart:

- **toobusy** — search `toobusy` in Manager (publisher `neobabae`). **v0.4.9 or newer.**
  Provides `toobusy MiniMax H3 Image Latent` and `toobusy MiniMax H3 Semantic Reference`.
  [github.com/nicekriss/toobusy](https://github.com/nicekriss/toobusy)
- **rgthree-comfy** — search `rgthree` in Manager. Used for the Stage 2 group switch.

The six LoadImage nodes will show missing files on first open. Those are the
author's local inputs — point them at your own images.

---

If a loader below shows `MISSING`, download the file from its link and place it in the displayed folder **without changing the filename**.

# 🎬 2BZ Workflow

**Created and produced by:** Too Busy Grasshopper (2BZ)

**YouTube:** [@toobusyAI](https://www.youtube.com/@toobusyAI)

## Inspiration & Original Post

This workflow was inspired by the original MiniMax H3 image-editing experiment shared on Reddit:

[MiniMax H3 as an image editor — 6 edits in one shot](https://www.reddit.com/r/StableDiffusion/comments/1vr1i18/minimax_h3_as_image_editor_6_edits_in_one_shot_at/)

The workflow expands that idea into a reusable two-stage character-sheet system with separate identity/outfit setup, optional pose and prop controls, and a final 16:9 composite.

This English edition is intended for public distribution. Please keep the creator credit and original inspiration link when sharing or modifying the workflow.

# Decide Whether to Run Stage 2

**Default OFF:** Queue generates only the Stage 1 face + outfit front / side / back sheet.

## To use Stage 2
1. Load a pose image in **⑦ Stage 2 Inputs**.
2. Enable only the optional props or environment references you need.
3. Choose the panel count and, for three panels, the fixed layout.
4. Add optional English panel requests in **⑧ Stage 2 Panel Requests**.
5. Turn ON the `Enable STAGE2_SWITCH` click toggle and Queue.

Turn the same switch OFF when you want to run Stage 1 only again.
